notes: I scanned Azure DocumentDB documentation (quickstarts, vector-search, indexing, security, sharding, autoscale, monitoring) and related Microsoft guidance. Most of the sample app's best-practice priors are supported by Azure DocumentDB docs (connection string via env, singleton MongoClient, index/explain usage, vector-index configuration, sharding guidance, autoscale, upsert idempotent seeding, monitoring). The notable contradiction is client writeConcern/readConcern: Azure maps or ignores client writeConcern and you should design around the service consistency model rather than expecting driver-level w=majority to be honored. Three prior beliefs had no clear Azure DocumentDB page that explicitly states them (keep PHI out of logs in product docs, explicit schema_version mandate, and provenance metadata for LLM outputs) so they are recorded as prior_knowledge_only with the searches attempted.
